name: Web App Intrusion
description: Web application attack — SQLi, RCE, webshell, server compromise.
initialKeyQuestions: What web application or endpoint was targeted?
What was the attack technique (SQLi, RCE, file upload, SSRF)?
Was a webshell or backdoor installed?
What OS commands were executed by the web process?
Did the attacker pivot from the web server to internal systems?
What data was accessed or exfiltrated?
Has the vulnerability been patched or the system isolated?

initialNextSteps.action: Snapshot the compromised web server, then isolate it from the network
initialNextSteps.rationale: Preserve evidence before isolation; prevent further exploitation
initialNextSteps.pointer: VM snapshot or disk image first, then firewall/EDR isolation

initialNextSteps.action: Search for webshells across the web root and all upload/temp directories
Collect and archive web server access logs (Apache/Nginx/IIS/WAF) for the full attack window
initialNextSteps.rationale: Access logs are the primary evidence source

initialNextSteps.action: Review OS process execution for suspicious child processes spawned by the web worker
initialNextSteps.rationale: RCE/webshell activity appears as the web process spawning cmd/bash/python
initialNextSteps.pointer: Sysmon EID 1, Auditd execve, Security EID 4688 filtered by ParentImage

findingsSeeds: OS commands executed by web process
Pivot from web server to internal systems

reportFraming.summaryPrompt: Summarize the web-app intrusion, exploited vulnerability, and remediation for the app team and executive.

synthesisHint: This is a web-app-intrusion case — prioritize T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application, T1505.003 Server Software Component: Web Shell, T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter, and T1071 Application Layer Protocol (C2).
